note: RFS editions. Fall 2026 is transcribed from ycombinator.com/rfs directly (server-rendered, primary source). Earlier editions are not served in the page HTML (they load client-side and the Wayback Machine was unreachable from this machine), so they are reconstructed from secondary sources, each named per edition. Edition attribution between Winter 2025 and Spring 2025 is inconsistent across secondary sources and is flagged where it matters. Winter 2022 through Winter 2024 are absent because YC published no RFS in that window: the list in force was the 2018 edition, and YC's own Feb 2024 blog post describes that refresh as its first since 2018.

editions.label: Fall 2026
editions.framing: "AI is moving into the physical world." YC frames the batch around startups rebuilding the systems that power the real world — education, healthcare, defense, finance, infrastructure and work itself — and notes it includes, for the first time, a request from the sitting U.S. Secretary of the Army.

items.d: A product that adaptively teaches young children to read, write and do arithmetic at the quality of a devoted private tutor, at consumer scale — the on-ramp to a Diamond Age-style Primer.

items.a: Daniel P. Driscoll, US Secretary of the Army
items.d: Low-cost interceptors and anything that lowers cost per kill; next-gen sensors, payloads and hardware that plug into the Army's open system architecture; drones, resilient logistics, advanced manufacturing, survivable in extreme climates.

A cloud built for 'small software' — purpose-built tools with one or a handful of users — where deploying and sharing is as easy as a Google Doc, solving auth, permissions and safe sharing of arbitrary code.
AI that goes multiplayer the way Docs and Figma did: teams and agents working in a shared space rather than each person in a private chat box.
Moving compute offshore — siting data centers at sea to escape land, power and cooling constraints.

items.t: AI-Powered Consumer Products for 1 Billion People
items.d: Consumer AI at billion-user scale rather than prosumer niches.
Products for the demographic inversion — care, monitoring, companionship and administration for old age.

items.t: New Operating Systems for the Physical World
items.d: Control and coordination layers for physical systems — the software substrate under robots, facilities and infrastructure.

items.t: The Best Time to Build in Crypto
items.d: Crypto reframed post-regulation, after two years of near-total absence from the batches.
Capture and structuring of physical-world data — the training substrate embodied models are short of.
Proof-of-humanity infrastructure as generated content and agents saturate the network.
Compliance rebuilt for a world where both the filer and the reviewer are models.
APIs that repair and adapt themselves, so agent-to-software integration stops breaking.

editions.label: Summer 2026
editions.source: Secondary: thevccorner.com compilation of the Summer 2026 edition
editions.framing: Space, semiconductors and hardware supply chain appear as first-class requests alongside AI-native services. Three of fifteen requests are chip- or space-hardware requests.

items.d: AI and robotics to cut chemical use while raising yield.
Own the service business and staff it with AI, rather than selling tools to the incumbent firm.
Genomics plus AI for individualized diagnosis and treatment.
Extract and structure scattered company knowledge so agents can use it.
Defense against coordinated drone swarms using distributed systems.
Let users reshape software interfaces via AI without engineering.
Inference chips designed for the space environment and radiation tolerance.
Compress physical part manufacturing and hardware iteration cycles.
Manufacturing infrastructure that makes lunar operations economically viable.
Silicon optimized for agent loops rather than single-shot inference.
Replace entrenched legacy software with AI-native alternatives, domain by domain.
Machine-readable interfaces and APIs built for agents as the user.
Let early teams land enterprise pilots and deals fast.
Real-time tracking and compliance for semiconductor manufacturing.

items.t: The AI Operating System for Companies
items.d: Unify company data sources into one continuously learning intelligence layer.

editions.label: Spring 2026
editions.source: Secondary: the-ai-corner.com, vccafe.com, inc.com coverage of the Spring 2026 edition
editions.framing: Seven requests, six of them explicitly AI. Two are physical-economy requests (metal mills, guidance for physical work); one is stablecoin financial services tied to named legislation.

items.d: Agentic tooling for deciding what to build, not just writing the code.
Funds built agent-first, analysing filings, calls and markets at machine scale — the argument being AI is where quant was in the 1980s.
Rebuild agency and consulting workflows with AI rather than sell software to them.
Compliant yield-bearing accounts and cross-border infrastructure on stablecoins, with the GENIUS and CLARITY Acts named as the opening.
Agencies need AI to process the volume the private sector now generates; sticky customers, large contracts.
Software-defined aluminium and steel mills with AI planning and modern automation, to cut lead times and energy cost.
Multimodal models plus wearables that see, reason and coach physical tasks in real time.

editions.label: Fall 2025
editions.source: Secondary: the-ai-corner.com and inc.com coverage of the Fall 2025 edition
editions.framing: All six requests are AI-at-the-core. The first is about the physical labour shortage created by the AI build-out itself.

items.t: Reskilling Workers for the AI Economy
items.d: A new vocational school for the AI build-out: electricians, HVAC techs, welders, tied to the government AI Action Plan's worker-first retraining funding.
Video models at near-zero marginal cost become a basic building block of software.
Infrastructure for fan-out agent workflows and 'agentic mapreduce' over large corpora.
The Salesforce/ServiceNow moment repeated: systems of record with AI embedded throughout.
Optimize revenue per employee; small teams beating incumbents on speed.
Intelligence is good enough to treat an agent like a person, and token cost is falling ~10x/year.

editions.label: Summer 2025
editions.source: Secondary: vccafe.com Part 3 compilation; the same 14 topics were indexed by Exa in May 2025
editions.framing: Fourteen topics, dominated by 'full-stack AI' — own the firm instead of selling to it. Two robotics entries appear for the first time as their own requests.

items.d: Start your own AI-staffed company to take on slow-moving incumbents (e.g. your own law firm, not an agent sold to law firms).
As coding gets cheap, taste and UX become the scarce input; designers should found.
Business phone calls have not changed in 100 years.
Drug discovery, chemical optimization, metals and mining, power grid.
Email, scheduling and tasks handled without supervision.
Attack the $1T+ in US healthcare administrative cost.
Multimodal, adaptive, real-time feedback.
Build the software foundation for the 'ChatGPT moment' in robotics.
Reshape how 1.5 billion students learn.
Commercial-grade AI security for the ~$20B home security market.
Let non-technical employees build their own automation agents.
Deep, open-ended research that may take years to commercialize.
Hands-free email with summarization and drafting.
Unbiased personalized financial advice at near-zero cost.

editions.label: Spring 2025
editions.source: Secondary: vccafe.com 'Extended Requests for Startups 2025 list' (6 Feb 2025). Caution: several sources file some of these items under Winter 2025 instead; the boundary between the two editions is not clean in secondary coverage.
editions.framing: Fourteen requests, almost all agent-and-infrastructure shaped. First appearance of data centers as an explicit YC request.

items.d: An OS layer with per-app data permissions, shared user memory, vetting and payments.
Build data centers faster and cheaper — power, cooling, materials procurement, and the software to construct and operate them.
Automate compliance by parsing regulatory documents and financial statements.
Rethink document creation and distribution for e-signature, with AI templates and voice agents.
Turn web and desktop workflows into usable APIs via agents.
Personalized assistants doing real knowledge work — accounting, tutoring.
The tooling and infrastructure layer for building and deploying agents.
Generalist developers managing teams of coding agents.
The Red Hat model applied to open-source AI tooling.

items.t: AI Coding Agents for Hardware-Optimized Code
items.d: Generate hardware-optimized kernels to make Nvidia alternatives viable.
Software whose primary customer is an agent, not a person.
Automate a category of work entirely rather than make humans faster.
A request for a kind of founder rather than a product.
Attack rising inference cost through better software and GPU utilization.

editions.label: Winter 2025
editions.source: Secondary and PARTIAL: medium/review.exe and swipefile coverage name these items; no complete list of the Winter 2025 edition was recoverable from this machine without the Wayback Machine.
editions.framing: The most politically inflected edition: reshoring, government, public safety, jobs. Physical-world and state-facing requests dominate; this is the edition where 'US-based manufacturing' first appears.

items.d: AI applied to construction and engineering processes.
AI to automate government administrative work.
Computer vision for detecting suspicious activity; better emergency response.
Reshoring via robotic systems and machine learning for automated production.
Restated jobs-creation request.
Named in coverage of this edition alongside reshoring.
Named in coverage of this edition.
Additional Winter 2025 items exist that could not be verified from an accessible source; treat this edition as partially reconstructed.

editions.label: Summer 2024
editions.framing: The first RFS refresh since 2018, and the last edition before YC moved to a per-batch cadence. Twenty categories. Robotics, defense, space, reshoring and climate all appear; agents do not appear as a category at all, and there is no 'physical AI' language yet.

items.d: ML for robotic systems.

items.t: Using machine learning to simulate the physical world
items.d: Learned physics simulation.
Defense and security.
Reshoring production.
Commercial space.
Environmental and sustainability technology.
Monetizing open source.
Immersive and spatial platforms.
Modern ERP alternatives.

items.t: Developer tools inspired by internal tools
items.d: Productize internal engineering tooling.
Interpretable systems.

items.t: LLMs for manual back office processes
items.d: Legacy enterprise back-office automation.
AI-driven software construction.
Stablecoin-based financial services.
Cancer breakthroughs.
Bio foundation models.

items.t: The managed service organization model for healthcare
items.d: Restructured care delivery.
Direct provider connections.
Integration between enterprise systems.
Specialized models instead of giant generic ones.

editions.label: Winter 2022 – Winter 2024
editions.source: Inference from YC's own Feb 2024 post plus contemporaneous press (TechCrunch, 14 Feb 2024) describing that post as the first RFS refresh since 2018.
editions.framing: No batch-specific RFS existed for these six batches (W22, S22, W23, S23, W24 and the run-up to S24). The list in force dated from 2018. Anything the batches did in this window was therefore not RFS-directed — which makes the 2022–23 batch composition a clean control against the post-2024 editions.
